The package declares evidence_status "insufficient": both assembled requirements (staff-026 and staff-033) register missing obligations for applicability, evidence closure, legal version reconciliation, independent meaning review and question-scope resolution, and the resolved concept "Benefit interaction" (overlap) is recorded as not covered by any applicable evidence requirement. The package is also truncated: budget.truncated is true (50 of 64 nodes, 216,183 of 262,144 bytes, reached_depth 3), and retrieval is truncated under a "retrieval_candidate_budget" omission — only 16 of 3,414 lexical candidate pages from a 19,090-page corpus were admitted, so other matching guidance pages lie outside this context.

Within that frozen, unreviewed scope, the selected ADM/DMG pages do support bounded observations about how the two benefits are linked in the captured guidance: ADM Chapter P5 treats a "DLA entitled person" as aged 16 or over entitled to either or both DLA components, and describes invitation of such persons to claim PIP on reaching 16 after 27.10.13 subject to a specified relevant date, with exceptions for terminal illness and for those admitted to hospital as in-patients under 18; no PIP claim may be made by a claimant who has not reached 16, whether or not they are entitled to DLA; a notification must explain that DLA entitlement will end if PIP is not claimed within the stated 28-day period. ADM Chapter P1 states PIP replaces DLA for working-age claimants, that first-time PIP entitlement requires being 16 or over and not in receipt of DLA, and that existing DLA claimants retain DLA until a PIP decision is made. DMG Chapter 61 records DLA's under-pensionable-age condition and child-relevant mobility component age thresholds. ADM/DMG memos captured for 2025 record that in Scotland child DLA's replacement is Child Disability Payment and PIP's is Adult Disability Payment, with claim rules on permanent moves from England and Wales. Separately, UC and SPC guidance treats entitlement to either DLA or PIP (or devolved equivalents) as triggering disabled-child additions.

These are captured source observations only. Dates in the text are as captured; capture dates are not publication, commencement or applicability dates, records are marked "unreviewed-specialist-review-required", and concept definitions are model-authored proposals. Within that frozen, unreviewed scope, the selected ADM/DMG pages do support bounded observations about how the two benefits are linked in the captured guidance: ADM Chapter P5 treats a "DLA entitled person" as aged 16 or over entitled to either or both DLA components, and describes invitation of such persons to claim PIP on reaching 16 after 27.10.13 subject to a specified relevant date, with exceptions for terminal illness and for those admitted to hospital as in-patients under 18; no PIP claim may be made by a claimant who has not reached 16, whether or not they are entitled to DLA; a notification must explain that DLA entitlement will end if PIP is not claimed within the stated 28-day period. ADM Chapter P1 states PIP replaces DLA for working-age claimants, that first-time PIP entitlement requires being 16 or over and not in receipt of DLA, and that existing DLA claimants retain DLA until a PIP decision is made. DMG Chapter 61 records DLA's under-pensionable-age condition and child-relevant mobility component age thresholds. ADM/DMG memos captured for 2025 record that in Scotland child DLA's replacement is Child Disability Payment and PIP's is Adult Disability Payment, with claim rules on permanent moves from England and Wales. Separately, UC and SPC guidance treats entitlement to either DLA or PIP (or devolved equivalents) as triggering disabled-child additions.
